notes: The whole source is 2371 × 1689 pixels. The full image was viewed once, then left half a and right half b once each, then only the 20 saved decision crops once each. No image delivery failed; there was no recrop and no reopening of a whole image or half.

Observation of content: an upper free-group chain and unfinished boundary calculation accompany a right-column condition (C_i), followed by labelled low-dimensional conditions and pi_0/pi_1/pi_2 notes. These are observations of what is written, not checked theorems.

No mathematical proof, independent re-proof, formal computation or mathematical background result was checked or invoked as a verified result during this reading. The checks list is intentionally empty. Apparent type/index inconsistencies prompted inspection of the ink only.

Potential author slips preserved: first chain index remains uncertain; the upper difference has unmatched parentheses; first s in c has a dotted i; the c-prime t row exposes only one horizontal relation stroke. No intended mathematical corrections have been supplied.

No explicit author question, date or title is visible. The lower-left 4 is treated as an archive sheet number, not as a manuscript folio. All uncertainty macros in reading.tex are reader uncertainties, not quotations of an author question.

The closing prose is read as “on n’exige pas que”; the earlier contextual suggestion “nécessaire” is not supported by the visible separate n/apostrophe sequence and descending g. NB has no visible full stops.

Faint regular background traces are visible. A narrow unforegrounded strip was cropped, rotated 90 degrees and enlarged once (crop 19); it yielded no securely recoverable complete typed word. It appears reversed/show-through-like. No front-face typescript or reused-typed sheet classification is established from this alone, and no invented unreadable word count is supplied.

H_drawing.tex was read before the parent corrected its association. Its own header identifies archive page 5 / PDF page 6, corresponding to a different scan. It was excluded from this collation and inventory; the x-loop in that file is not counted as missing or spurious scan 005 content. No other-page image or text was opened.

The side brace in C was retained after direct examination. The upper low bracket, two small lower sketches, detached cross-like mark, and final enclosing top/left stroke are literal geometric approximations. Their strokes and gaps are preserved without imposing a mathematical interpretation on stray marks.

The fixed-width enlargement makes very small isolated marks large and soft but cannot recover absent source pixels. No sharpening was used. All crops used Pillow autocontrast cutoff 0 and LANCZOS resizing; only the background strip was rotated.
The six vertical membership signs open downward. They have been encoded by rotating an ordinary membership sign clockwise through 90 degrees; C’s positive rotation gives the opposite visible opening.

Reader implementation correction before report: the existing unprimed label on the leftward chain arrow was retained, since its source label belongs below the shaft. H’s explicit overset placement remains a layout discrepancy.

One final textual comparison against C was completed after the image reading. Every substantive change in that diff has an issue entry; retained tiny-index doubts are logged at all four occurrences even when marked inline only once.

brief_feedback: The workflow was sufficient. A supplied H drawing had an incorrect page association; the parent supplied a metadata correction and it was excluded. A mandatory approximately 2200-pixel enlargement is oversized for the isolated chain mark and singleton stroke, adding display area rather than information; a source-pixel-based cap would be more efficient. The instruction not to infer reused typing from pale remnants was useful for the faint background.
